newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST--Italy PPI seen rising 0.42 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST--Italy PPI seen rising 0.42 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Italy's producer and wholesale prices are seen rising slightly in October, still feeling the pressure of the increase in oil prices after the summer, a Reuter poll of analysts showed on Tuesday.
They added that after the October data there should not be any further significant price pressure from oil this year.

Analysts polled said the increase in oil prices was only a temporary factor that should be phased out definitely in the December data and maybe even in November and, in any case, should not cause a significant rise in the year-on-year figure.

Analysts see PPI rising 0.25 percent monthly and 0.42 percent annually from 0.1 percent and 0.2 percent respectively in September 1996. In October 1995, producer prices were unchanged on a monthly basis and rose 7.9 percent year-on-year.

Wholesale prices are seen up 0.42 percent monthly and 1.6 percent annually from September's 0.4 percent rise monthly and 1.3 percent year-on-year. In October 1995, WPI rose 0.1 percent monthly and 10.8 percent annually.
Italy's national statistics body ISTAT will publish the final figures on Wednesday December 18.
